text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- European council to decide which countries will be part of the first single currency wave in May 1998.
-- French government to face further labour tensions from doctors, bank workers, road and air transport workers.
-- Britain's GEC in talks with Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere for possible alliance with the winner of a bid for Thomson-CSF, after government vetoes GEC bid for Thomson-CSF for security reasons.
-- France Telecom to cut prices by some nine percent on average in 1998, and by a yearly 4.5 percent through 2000.
-- Moody's ratings agency lowers its rating of Societe Generale to Aa3 from Aa2 despite the bank's 1996 4.5-billion-franc profit.
-- Boeing chairman Phil Condit says in an interview that Boeing expects synergies from its merger with McDonnell Douglas, to be implemented this summer.

-- Head of economic research institute Gama, Raymond Courbis, says in an interview he expects an economic growth of 1.9 percent only for 1997, adds he does not trust political promises made by governments.
-- French authorities to allow GEC to join forces with French buyer of Thomson-CSF, Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said.
